page: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running up to 3.9 GHz. The instance delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores, complemented by a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 256 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration covers AVX-512 extensions and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX with tile and int8 support). Local ephemeral capacity is provided via 7,600 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 50 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark measurements highlight high multi-core scaling and data ingestion capacity. In multi-threaded execution, the platform achieved top-decile results across stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Clang software compilation suites. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 393.15 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measured 208.57 GB/sec. The presence of AMX instructions enables elevated prompt-processing rates in CPU-driven large language model inference. Conversely, single-core execution profiles fall into average to moderate brackets, such as a mid-tier stress-ng single-core score.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8id.32xlarge consolidates extensive parallel compute and massive fast local storage within a single host, eliminating external block storage transfer bottlenecks. The primary tradeoff lies in the compute-oriented 2 GB RAM-per-thread allocation, which makes the instance unsuitable for memory-dense datasets requiring massive in-memory capacities. It is well-fitted for distributed build systems, large-scale CI/CD compilation, high-throughput caching, high-IOPS batch data processing, and CPU-based vector inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by a 128-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at up to 3.9 GHz, supported by 256 GB of DDR5 memory and 7,600 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 50 Gbps baseline network throughput, this system leverages AVX-512 and Intel AMX hardware acceleration to deliver top-tier multi-threaded compute, high memory bandwidth, and rapid I/O processing. While single-threaded performance operates within middle tiers and memory allocation is kept strictly at 2 GB per vCPU, its dense core architecture and integrated NVMe capacity provide efficient resource utilization without external disk latency. The c8id.32xlarge fits demanding software compilation pipelines, distributed databases, high-rate batch analytics, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
